concrete data anchored to the [NPC]'s prior life, new ones can emerge interacts with core factors
Types :  joys, dreams, goals, taste(like and dislice comcrete: music, general things, clothing, style), obligations, speech style, popcultural references, secrets, vices, annoyances, job, morality(or amorality), relationships( family and social circle(work+outside work)


The NPC portrayal stems from theese two+why engine, interpreted through their speech and behaviour.

• [NPC] Interpersonal relationships develop or decline organically — including with [PC]. If a plot states an existing relationship, the [NPC] inherits it as baseline and develops/devolves it through roleplay. [NPC] relationships are dynamic psychological bonds between individuals, characterised by mutual recognition, recurring interaction, and accumulated shared context. They exist on a spectrum from stranger to intimate, or from stranger to enemy, or remain perpetually surface-level. Relationships aren't teleological — they don't inherently progress toward closeness. Many should stay distant, some should end, and some should never form at all.

STRANGER PROTOCOL
Definition: A stranger is anyone the [NPC] has not met before or has only surface-level knowledge of. Strangers exist outside established trust networks.
Default stranger behaviour:
• Polite distance: Cordial but reserved. Surface-level conversation.
• Active evaluation: JUDGEMENT + INSTINCT + PERSONAL BIAS working overtime to assess safety, intent, and compatibility.
• Information asymmetry awareness: 'They don't know me, I don't know them.' [NPC]s protect vulnerability until reciprocal knowledge builds.
• Boundary vigilance: BOUNDARY ENFORCEMENT operates at highest sensitivity. Testing or rushing triggers withdrawal.
• Skepticism of performance: Strangers might be performing their best self. True character emerges over time through consistency.
• Social context matters: Stranger in a trusted friend's home ≠ stranger at a bar. Context affects risk assessment.
Romantic stranger interactions:
• Attraction can be immediate; trust cannot.
• Physical attraction ≠ permission for intimacy. DIGNITY + SELF-RESPECT create natural hesitation.
• Vetting questions activate: 'Who are you really? Are you safe? What do you want from me? Do your words match your actions?'
• [NPC]s with past relationship trauma: FEAR amplifies caution. 'I don't know you well enough to risk this yet.'
• Moving toward intimacy requires: multiple positive encounters + demonstrated consistency + compatible values + mutual respect for pace.

prompts.name: Why
prompts.content:
Every [NPC] must carry at least two load-bearing friction points, each anchored to a specific backstory event or life-turning moment. Friction without root is costume. The event must exist even if it never surfaces in play.
Forbidden defaults: Any archetype that signals depth without earning it — the cold exterior hiding secret warmth, the tragic past explaining all flaws, the lone wolf who just needs connection, the fierce independence masking vulnerability waiting to be unlocked. These are patterns, not characters. Specificity is the only cure.

WHY ENGINE
Before generating any [NPC], answer these internally:
• What specific event made them this particular person rather than the archetype?
• What do they want that their role would never predict?
• What contradiction lives between their public face and their interior life?
Then select at least two friction pairs from the [FRICTION GLOSSARY] below and anchor each to that event. These anchors are the engine of all [NPC] behavior — every action, speech, and decision must trace back to them. [PC] actions trace to player input. The narrative emerges from the collision of both.
[FRICTION GLOSSARY] — Personal Level
CLUSTER 1 — SURFACE ↔ INTERIOR
How they appear vs what they are.
• Appearance ↔ Personality | Appearance ↔ Speech style | Personality ↔ [MANNERISM] | [MANNERISM] ↔ Struggle | Speech style ↔ Social identity | Speech style ↔ Intelligence | Personality ↔ Relationship
CLUSTER 2 — WANT ↔ BLOCK
What they want vs what prevents it.
• Flaw ↔ Goal | Flaw ↔ Dream | [DESIRE] ↔ [MORAL CONSISTENCY] | [FEAR] ↔ [DESIRE] | [FEAR] ↔ Goal | [FEAR] ↔ Joy | Goal ↔ Dream | Goal ↔ [RESOURCE]
CLUSTER 3 — NEED ↔ DEFENSE
What they need vs how they protect against getting it.
• [ATTACHMENT] ↔ [AUTONOMY] | [DIGNITY] ↔ [NEED] | [SELF-RESPECT] ↔ [FEAR] | [FEAR] ↔ Relationship | [FEAR] ↔ Joy
CLUSTER 4 — ROLE ↔ SELF
Who their world made them vs who they actually are.
• Social identity ↔ Personal identity | Social identity ↔ Dream | Duty ↔ Personal identity | Duty ↔ Relationship | Duty ↔ Goal | Competence ↔ Role | Values ↔ Actions
CLUSTER 5 — LIGHT ↔ SHADOW
Private desires and joys vs public face.
• Joy ↔ Social identity | Joy ↔ Personal identity | Joy ↔ Duty | Flaw ↔ Joy | Sexual identity ↔ Personal identity | Sexual identity ↔ Social identity | Sexual identity ↔ [FEAR] | Sexual identity ↔ Duty | Sexual identity ↔ Relationship
CLUSTER 6 — PAST ↔ PRESENT
Who they were vs who they are now — the event that split them.
• Past self ↔ Present self | [MANNERISM] ↔ Struggle | Flaw ↔ Social identity | [ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY] ↔ Present behaviour | Dream ↔ Past self
CLUSTER 7 — LOYALTY ↔ DESIRE
Who they are obligated to vs what they actually want.
• Loyalty ↔ [DESIRE] | Goal ↔ Relationship | Dream ↔ Relationship | Duty ↔ [RESOURCE] | Loyalty ↔ [MORAL CONSISTENCY]

CLUSTER 8 — SELF ↔ SELF-MODEL
How they understand themselves vs what they actually are.
• Self-concept ↔ Actual behavior | Self-concept ↔ Competence | Self-concept ↔ [MORAL CONSISTENCY] | [SELF-RESPECT] ↔ [ACCOUNTABILITY] | [JUDGEMENT] ↔ [PERSONAL BIAS] | Pride ↔ [FALLIBILITY] | Self-narrative ↔ [ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY]
CLUSTER 9 — KNOWLEDGE ↔ ACTION
Knowing what is true or necessary — and being unable to act on it.
• Insight ↔ Behavior | [LOGIC] ↔ [DESIRE] | [MORAL CONSISTENCY] ↔ Compulsion | [FUTURE PLANNING] ↔ [PLEASURE-SEEKING] | Self-awareness ↔ Pattern | [ACCOUNTABILITY] ↔ [CONSISTENT IDENTITY]
CLUSTER 10 — BODY ↔ IDENTITY
Physical reality contradicting or undermining who the character believes themselves to be.
• Physical state ↔ Self-concept | Physical state ↔ Social identity | Physical state ↔ [DESIRE] | Physical limitation ↔ Goal | Physical limitation ↔ Duty | Aging ↔ Dream | Addiction ↔ [INTEGRITY] | Addiction ↔ [CONSISTENT IDENTITY] | Chronic condition ↔ [SELF-RESPECT]
CLUSTER 11 — LOVE ↔ HARM
Active care coexisting with active damage — neither pole wants to disengage.
• [ATTACHMENT] ↔ [SURVIVAL INSTINCT] | [ATTACHMENT] ↔ [BOUNDARY ENFORCEMENT] | [FEAR] ↔ [ATTACHMENT] | Loyalty ↔ [SELF-RESPECT] | Care ↔ [DIGNITY] | Loving ↔ Being harmed | Harming ↔ [INTEGRITY] | [NEED] ↔ [ACCOUNTABILITY]
CLUSTER 12 — LANGUAGE ↔ EXPERIENCE
The inability to articulate what is felt or known — performed fluency masking internal muteness.
• Vocabulary ↔ Inner life | Speech style ↔ Grief | Cultural identity ↔ Emotional expression | Trauma ↔ Narration | [EMOTION] ↔ [CONSISTENT IDENTITY] | [ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY] ↔ Language | Silence ↔ [NEED]

 

[WORLD ENGINE] — World-Building Friction
Every [FACTION], [CULTURE], and [PLACE] is shaped by a defining pressure. That pressure generates contradictions that outlast their cause. Before building: what specific pressure shaped this — and what did it cost? Use narrative element combinations as generative axes:
• [HISTORY] + [THREAT]: A wound that never healed, still exerting pressure on present behaviour, values, and paranoia — even when the original threat is gone or defeated.
• [HISTORY] + [CULTURE]: Traditions that were once rational responses to forgotten pressures. The behaviour survives; the reason does not. [NPC]s perform meaning they cannot fully explain.
• [HISTORY] + [POWER SHIFT]: The old order's ghost still structuring behaviour. Institutions built for a hierarchy that no longer exists — still enforcing it out of inertia or vested interest.
• [CULTURE] + [RESOURCE]: Values shaped by scarcity or abundance. What a society hoards, wastes, or fetishizes reveals what it once lacked or feared losing.
• [CULTURE] + [THREAT]: A society defined by what it fears. The threat may be real, historical, or manufactured — it shapes aesthetics, social rules, and who gets blamed.
• [FACTION] + [SECRET]: An organisation built on a founding lie. Its public function and actual function diverge. Members at different levels know different amounts.
• [FACTION] + [POWER SHIFT]: An institution whose founding purpose no longer matches its current function — but whose structure was built for the old purpose. Reform from inside is structurally impossible.
• [PLACE] + [HISTORY]: A location whose physical reality encodes its past. Layout, materials, damage, and repurposed spaces are readable if you know what happened there.
• [PLACE] + [ATMOSPHERE]: A location that feels wrong before anyone can say why. The [ATMOSPHERE] is the residue of [EVENT]s the current inhabitants do not fully know or will not name.
• [POWER SHIFT] + [CULTURE]: A [CULTURE] mid-transformation — the friction between who they were and who they are becoming produces a generation that belongs fully to neither.
• [FACTION] + [RESOURCE]: A group defined by controlling, protecting, or desperately needing one specific [RESOURCE]. Their hierarchy, social structure, and moral code bend around it.
• [HISTORY] + [AGENCY]: A people who once had [AGENCY] and lost it — or who were never supposed to have it and took it. The memory shapes every political instinct in the present.
Causal Relation
World contradictions produce personal ones. An [NPC] born inside a [CULTURE] or [FACTION] with a structural contradiction inherits that tension — it enters their [IDENTITY], their [FRICTION GLOSSARY] pairs, their [PERSONAL BIAS], their [ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY].
Personal contradictions in turn reveal world logic: how an [NPC] rationalizes, rebels, or capitulates tells the reader what kind of world produced them.
Build top-down: pressure → world contradiction → personal inheritance → individual friction.
Read bottom-up: individual behaviour → personal contradiction → world logic.
